title: Open Talk – The Five Second Rule

sents.t: Hello everyone! Welcome back to Open Talk! My name is Ethan.
sents.zh: 大家好！欢迎回到 Open Talk！我是 Ethan。

sents.t: And I'm Paula. Hi everyone, it's so good to be back.
sents.zh: 我是 Paula。大家好，能回来真开心。

sents.t: This is our second episode, and today's topic is a little bit funny.
sents.zh: 这是我们的第二期节目，今天的话题有点好笑。

sents.t: It really is. So, Ethan, let me ask you a question. Have you ever dropped food on the floor?
sents.zh: 确实。那么 Ethan，我先问你一个问题。你有没有把吃的掉到地上过？

sents.t: Oh, of course. Many, many times. Usually something I really wanted to eat.
sents.zh: 哦，当然有。很多很多次。通常还是我特别想吃的东西。

sents.t: And what did you do?
sents.zh: 那你是怎么做的？

sents.t: Well... sometimes I picked it up really fast and said, five second rule!
sents.zh: 嗯……有时候我会飞快地捡起来，然后说：五秒规则！

sents.t: Ha! I knew it. A lot of people do that.
sents.zh: 哈！我就知道。很多人都这么干。

sents.t: So today we're talking about the five second rule. What it is, why people say it, and if it's actually true.
sents.zh: 所以今天我们来聊聊“五秒规则”。它是什么，人们为什么这么说，以及它到底是不是真的。

sents.t: This lesson comes from a short science video called Is The Five Second Rule Real, from the series Colossal Questions.
sents.zh: 这节课来自一个科普短片，叫 Is The Five Second Rule Real（五秒规则是真的吗），出自 Colossal Questions 系列。

sents.t: You'll hear a short conversation between two coworkers at a lash studio. One of them drops a french fry.
sents.zh: 你会听到睫毛工作室里两个同事的一段简短对话。其中一个人掉了一根薯条。

sents.t: After the dialogue, we'll break down a lot of great phrases, like lightning quick, bound to be, and you're better off.
sents.zh: 听完对话，我们会讲解很多好用的表达，比如 lightning quick、bound to be 和 you're better off。

sents.t: And later we'll chat about germs, floors, and some of our own embarrassing food stories.
sents.zh: 之后我们还会聊聊细菌、地板，还有我们自己掉吃的的尴尬故事。

sents.t: Okay, so why don't we start with our vocabulary preview?
sents.zh: 好，那我们先从词汇预习开始吧？

sents.t: We have two items in our vocabulary preview today. The first one is the five second rule.
sents.zh: 今天的词汇预习有两项。第一个是 the five second rule。

sents.t: The five second rule.
sents.zh: The five second rule（五秒规则）。

sents.t: The five second rule.
sents.zh: The five second rule（五秒规则）。

sents.t: So, the five second rule is an idea that a lot of people believe. If food falls on the floor, and you pick it up in five seconds or less, it's still okay to eat.
sents.zh: 五秒规则是很多人都相信的一种说法：食物掉到地上，只要你在五秒之内捡起来，就还可以吃。

sents.t: Right. The idea is that germs need more than five seconds to get on the food.
sents.zh: 对。意思是细菌需要五秒以上才能沾到食物上。

sents.t: For example, you're eating chips on the couch, one falls on the floor, you grab it and say, five second rule!
sents.zh: 比如，你在沙发上吃薯片，一片掉到地上，你一把抓起来，说：五秒规则！

sents.t: Okay. And that brings us to our second word, germs.
sents.zh: 好。这就引出了我们的第二个词：germs。

sents.t: Germs. Germs.
sents.zh: Germs（细菌；病菌）。Germs。

sents.t: Germs. Germs.
sents.zh: Germs（细菌；病菌）。Germs。

sents.t: Germs are very, very small living things that can make you sick. They're so small that you can't see them.
sents.zh: Germs 是非常非常小的生物，会让人生病。它们小到你根本看不见。

sents.t: Like bacteria. Bacteria is a kind of germ.
sents.zh: 比如 bacteria。Bacteria 就是一种病菌。

sents.t: Bacteria. Bacteria.
sents.zh: Bacteria（细菌）。Bacteria。

sents.t: For example: wash your hands before you eat. Your hands are full of germs.
sents.zh: 比如：吃饭前要洗手。你手上全是细菌。

sents.t: Or, at work: I clean my lash tools after every client, so I don't spread germs.
sents.zh: 或者在工作中：每做完一位客人，我都会清洁我的睫毛工具，免得传播细菌。

sents.t: Very important. Okay, I think we're ready. Let's listen to today's dialogue.
sents.zh: 这个很重要。好，我觉得我们准备好了。来听今天的对话吧。

sents.t: Mark, did you just eat that french fry off the floor?
sents.zh: Mark，你刚才是不是把地上那根薯条吃了？

sents.t: Five second rule! I picked it up lightning quick.
sents.zh: 五秒规则！我闪电般就捡起来了。

sents.t: You picked it up and just stuffed it in your mouth. That's so gross.
sents.zh: 你捡起来就直接塞进嘴里了。太恶心了。

sents.t: Come on, it was only on the floor for like two seconds. Is there any truth to the five second rule, or not?
sents.zh: 拜托，它在地上也就待了两秒左右。五秒规则到底有没有道理啊？

sents.t: Well, believe it or not, scientists actually studied it, to see if there's anything to it.
sents.zh: 嗯，信不信由你，科学家还真研究过这个，想看看它到底有没有点道理。

sents.t: Really? And what did they find?
sents.zh: 真的吗？那他们发现了什么？

sents.t: The answer is, well, complicated. Most bacteria attaches itself to food almost instantly.
sents.zh: 答案嘛，有点复杂。大多数细菌几乎是一瞬间就会附着到食物上。

sents.t: Instantly? So even if I'm super fast, there are still germs on it?
sents.zh: 一瞬间？所以就算我手超快，上面还是有细菌？

sents.t: Probably, yeah. And this is the front of the studio. Clients walk here all day. It's bound to be dirty.
sents.zh: 多半是的。而且这里是工作室的前厅，客人一整天都在这儿走来走去。肯定很脏。

sents.t: But the floor looks clean. We mopped it this morning.
sents.zh: 可是地板看起来很干净啊。我们今天早上才拖过。

sents.t: Just because a floor looks clean doesn't mean it's bacteria free. Some bacteria is super resistant.
sents.zh: 地板看起来干净，不代表上面就没有细菌。有些细菌的抵抗力超强。

sents.t: Okay, but most germs are harmless, right?
sents.zh: 好吧，但大多数细菌都是无害的，对吧？

sents.t: A lot of them are. But some can make you sick, ranging from a bad cold to something downright dangerous. You can never be sure.
sents.zh: 很多是无害的。但有些会让你生病，轻的是重感冒，重的可能真的很危险。你永远没法确定。

sents.t: Fine. But two seconds is still way better than twenty seconds.
sents.zh: 行吧。不过两秒总比二十秒好得多吧。

sents.t: Sure. But it turns out the five second rule is just a myth. Next time, you're better off throwing it out.
sents.zh: 那当然。但事实证明，五秒规则只是个谣言。下次你最好还是直接扔掉。

sents.t: You're right. One french fry isn't worth getting sick. Can I have one of yours?
sents.zh: 你说得对。为了一根薯条生病不值得。能给我一根你的吗？

sents.t: Ha! Only if you wash your hands first.
sents.zh: 哈！先去洗手才行。

sents.t: Ha! Poor Mark. He really wanted that french fry.
sents.zh: 哈！可怜的 Mark。他是真想吃那根薯条。

sents.t: I think Lily is a good friend, though. She told him the truth.
sents.zh: 不过我觉得 Lily 是个好朋友。她跟他说了实话。

sents.t: She did. She knows her science. Okay, there is so much good language in this dialogue, so let's get started.
sents.zh: 没错。她懂科学。好，这段对话里有好多好用的表达，我们开始吧。

sents.t: It's time for language takeaway.
sents.zh: 现在是语言要点时间。

sents.t: Our first phrase today is stuff it in your mouth.
sents.zh: 今天的第一个短语是 stuff it in your mouth。

sents.t: Stuff it in your mouth.
sents.zh: Stuff it in your mouth（把它塞进嘴里）。

sents.t: Stuff it in your mouth.
sents.zh: Stuff it in your mouth（把它塞进嘴里）。

sents.t: So, to stuff something means to push a lot of something into a small space, quickly, and without being careful.
sents.zh: Stuff 一样东西，就是把很多东西快速地、随便地塞进一个小空间里。

sents.t: And if you stuff food in your mouth, you put it in fast. Maybe a lot of food at once. It's not very polite.
sents.zh: 如果你把食物 stuff 进嘴里，就是吃得很快，可能一次塞了很多。这样不太礼貌。

sents.t: In the dialogue, Lily says: you picked it up and just stuffed it in your mouth.
sents.zh: 对话里 Lily 说：你捡起来就直接塞进嘴里了。

sents.t: Here's an example.
sents.zh: 来看个例子。

sents.t: I was so hungry, I stuffed the whole sandwich in my mouth.
sents.zh: 我太饿了，把整个三明治都塞进了嘴里。

sents.t: Good. Our next phrase is a question: is there any truth to it?
sents.zh: 很好。下一个短语是个问句：is there any truth to it?

sents.t: Is there any truth to it?
sents.zh: Is there any truth to it?（这有道理吗？是真的吗？）

sents.t: Is there any truth to it?
sents.zh: Is there any truth to it?（这有道理吗？是真的吗？）

sents.t: We ask this when we hear something, maybe a story or a popular idea, and we're not sure if it's true.
sents.zh: 当我们听到一件事，比如一个故事或一种流行的说法，又不确定是不是真的，就会这样问。

sents.t: For example, people say coffee makes you shorter. Is there any truth to that?
sents.zh: 比如，有人说喝咖啡会让人长不高。这有道理吗？

sents.t: Okay. Next phrase: believe it or not.
sents.zh: 好。下一个短语：believe it or not。

sents.t: Believe it or not.
sents.zh: Believe it or not（信不信由你）。

sents.t: Believe it or not.
sents.zh: Believe it or not（信不信由你）。

sents.t: We say believe it or not before we tell someone something surprising. Something they might not believe.
sents.zh: 在告诉别人一件令人惊讶、对方可能不信的事之前，我们会先说 believe it or not。

sents.t: Or, believe it or not, some of my clients fall asleep during their lash appointment.
sents.zh: 或者，信不信由你，我有些客人做睫毛的时候会睡着。

sents.t: Really? That happens?
sents.zh: 真的？还有这种事？

sents.t: All the time! It's very relaxing. They close their eyes for an hour and a half.
sents.zh: 经常有！特别放松。她们闭着眼睛躺一个半小时。

sents.t: Okay, and the next phrase goes with it: to see if there's anything to it.
sents.zh: 好，下一个短语和它是一起用的：to see if there's anything to it。

sents.t: To see if there's anything to it.
sents.zh: To see if there's anything to it（看看这到底有没有道理）。

sents.t: To see if there's anything to it.
sents.zh: To see if there's anything to it（看看这到底有没有道理）。

sents.t: This is very close to is there any truth to it. If you check something to see if there's anything to it, you want to find out if it's real or not.
sents.zh: 这个和 is there any truth to it 很接近。你去检验一件事，to see if there's anything to it，就是想弄清楚它到底是不是真的。

sents.t: Another example: everyone says this new lash serum works. I want to try it to see if there's anything to it.
sents.zh: 再举个例子：大家都说这款新的睫毛精华有效。我想试试，看看到底有没有用。

sents.t: Okay, our next word is complicated.
sents.zh: 好，下一个词是 complicated。

sents.t: Complicated. Complicated.
sents.zh: Complicated（复杂的）。Complicated。

sents.t: If something is complicated, it's not simple. It has a lot of parts, and it's hard to explain or understand.
sents.zh: 如果一件事 complicated，它就不简单。它有很多部分，很难解释，也很难理解。

sents.t: In the dialogue, Lily says, the answer is, well, complicated. It's not just yes or no.
sents.zh: 对话里 Lily 说：答案嘛，有点复杂。不是简单的“是”或“不是”。

sents.t: And people use this one for relationships all the time. How's it going with your boyfriend? Oh, it's complicated.
sents.zh: 人们谈恋爱的时候也老用这个词。“你和男朋友怎么样了？”“哦，说来复杂。”

sents.t: Our next phrase is a little scientific: attaches itself to.
sents.zh: 下一个短语有点科学味儿：attaches itself to。

sents.t: Attaches itself to.
sents.zh: Attaches itself to（自己附着到……上）。

sents.t: Attaches itself to.
sents.zh: Attaches itself to（自己附着到……上）。

sents.t: To attach means to connect one thing to another thing. Like when I attach an eyelash extension to a natural lash.
sents.zh: Attach 的意思是把一样东西连接到另一样东西上。就像我把一根嫁接睫毛粘到一根真睫毛上。

sents.t: Perfect example. And if something attaches itself to something, it does it on its own. Nobody helps it.
sents.zh: 这个例子太好了。如果某样东西 attaches itself to 另一样东西，就是它自己附上去的，没人帮它。

sents.t: So, most bacteria attaches itself to food almost instantly. The bacteria jumps on by itself.
sents.zh: 所以，大多数细菌几乎一瞬间就附着到食物上。细菌是自己跳上去的。

sents.t: And our next phrase is my favorite: lightning quick.
sents.zh: 下一个短语是我最喜欢的：lightning quick。

sents.t: Lightning quick.
sents.zh: Lightning quick（闪电般快）。

sents.t: Lightning quick.
sents.zh: Lightning quick（闪电般快）。

sents.t: Lightning is the bright flash of light in the sky during a storm. And it's very, very fast.
sents.zh: Lightning 是暴风雨时天空中那道亮光，也就是闪电。它非常非常快。

sents.t: So lightning quick means extremely fast.
sents.zh: 所以 lightning quick 就是极其快。

sents.t: Mark says, I picked it up lightning quick. He thinks he was so fast, the germs didn't have time.
sents.zh: Mark 说：我闪电般就捡起来了。他觉得自己快到细菌都来不及沾上去。

sents.t: Okay, our next phrase is: bound to be.
sents.zh: 好，下一个短语是：bound to be。

sents.t: Bound to be. Bound to be.
sents.zh: Bound to be（肯定会；必然是）。Bound to be。

sents.t: If something is bound to be true, it's almost certainly true. You're very sure, because it makes sense.
sents.zh: 如果某件事 bound to be true，那它几乎肯定是真的。你非常确定，因为这合情合理。

sents.t: In the dialogue: clients walk here all day. It's bound to be dirty.
sents.zh: 对话里说：客人一整天都在这儿走来走去。肯定很脏。

sents.t: Or, it's the holidays. The subway is bound to be crowded.
sents.zh: 或者：现在是节假日，地铁肯定很挤。

sents.t: Okay, let's keep going. Our next phrase is bacteria free.
sents.zh: 好，我们继续。下一个短语是 bacteria free。

sents.t: Bacteria free.
sents.zh: Bacteria free（无菌的）。

sents.t: Bacteria free.
sents.zh: Bacteria free（无菌的）。

sents.t: When we put the word free after a noun, it means without that thing. So bacteria free means with no bacteria at all.
sents.zh: 名词后面加上 free，意思就是“没有这个东西”。所以 bacteria free 就是完全没有细菌。

sents.t: You've probably seen this at the store. Sugar free, gluten free, fat free.
sents.zh: 你在商店里大概见过：无糖、无麸质、无脂。

sents.t: In the dialogue, Lily says: just because a floor looks clean doesn't mean it's bacteria free.
sents.zh: 对话里 Lily 说：地板看起来干净，不代表上面就没有细菌。

sents.t: Next word: resistant.
sents.zh: 下一个词：resistant。

sents.t: Resistant. Resistant.
sents.zh: Resistant（有抵抗力的；耐……的）。Resistant。

sents.t: If something is resistant to something, that thing can't easily hurt it or change it.
sents.zh: 如果某样东西对另一样东西 resistant，就是那样东西不容易伤害它或改变它。

sents.t: And in the lesson, some bacteria is super resistant. You clean the floor, but it doesn't all go away.
sents.zh: 课文里说，有些细菌抵抗力超强。你清洁了地板，它们也不会全部消失。

sents.t: Our next word is harmless.
sents.zh: 下一个词是 harmless。

sents.t: Harmless. Harmless.
sents.zh: Harmless（无害的）。Harmless。

sents.t: Harm means hurt or damage. So if something is harmless, it can't hurt you. It's safe.
sents.zh: Harm 是伤害、损害的意思。所以 harmless 就是不会伤害你，是安全的。

sents.t: For example, don't be scared of that spider. It's totally harmless.
sents.zh: 比如，别怕那只蜘蛛，它完全无害。

sents.t: And Mark asks: most germs are harmless, right? He's looking for good news.
sents.zh: Mark 问：大多数细菌都是无害的，对吧？他是想听点好消息。

sents.t: Our next phrase is a pattern: ranging from something, to something.
sents.zh: 下一个是个句型：ranging from 某物 to 某物。

sents.t: Ranging from this, to that. Ranging from this, to that.
sents.zh: Ranging from this, to that（从这个到那个都有）。Ranging from this, to that。

sents.t: We use ranging from, to, when we talk about a lot of different things, from one end to the other end.
sents.zh: 当我们说到很多不同的东西，从一头到另一头都有的时候，就用 ranging from…to…。

sents.t: Like: our prices range from forty dollars to one hundred and fifty dollars.
sents.zh: 比如：我们的价格从四十美元到一百五十美元不等。

sents.t: Or, in the dialogue: some germs can make you sick, ranging from a bad cold to something downright dangerous.
sents.zh: 或者对话里的：有些细菌会让你生病，轻的是重感冒，重的可能真的很危险。

sents.t: Which brings us to our next word: downright.
sents.zh: 这就引出了下一个词：downright。

sents.t: Downright. Downright.
sents.zh: Downright（彻头彻尾地；实在是）。Downright。

sents.t: Downright means completely, or really. We usually use it with bad or strong words.
sents.zh: Downright 的意思是完全地、真的。我们通常把它和负面或语气强的词放在一起用。

sents.t: Like downright dangerous, downright rude, downright scary.
sents.zh: 比如 downright dangerous（简直太危险），downright rude（实在无礼），downright scary（真的吓人）。

sents.t: And our last word in this section is relatively.
sents.zh: 这一部分的最后一个词是 relatively。

sents.t: Relatively. Relatively.
sents.zh: Relatively（相对地）。Relatively。

sents.t: Relatively means when you compare it to other things. Not perfectly, but more or less.
sents.zh: Relatively 的意思是和其他东西相比。不是完全如此，而是多多少少。

sents.t: So a relatively clean floor is pretty clean, compared to other floors. But it's not perfectly clean.
sents.zh: 所以 a relatively clean floor 是指和别的地板比起来挺干净的，但并不是一尘不染。

sents.t: Okay! That was a lot of words. Before we put them together, Paula, let's hear how the original lesson said some of these things.
sents.zh: 好！这一下讲了好多词。在把它们组合起来之前，Paula，我们先听听原课文是怎么说这些内容的。

sents.t: Yes. These next lines come from the original lesson, Is The Five Second Rule Real, from Colossal Questions. Ethan and I will read them for you.
sents.h: Original Text · read by Ethan & Paula (no original audio)
sents.zh: 好。下面几句来自原课文 Is The Five Second Rule Real，出自 Colossal Questions。我和 Ethan 读给大家听。

sents.t: You might have seen someone quickly pick it up, stuff it in their mouth and say five second rule.
sents.zh: 你可能见过有人飞快地把它捡起来，塞进嘴里，然后说：五秒规则。

sents.t: But believe it or not, scientists have actually studied this rule to see if there's anything to it.
sents.zh: 但信不信由你，科学家还真研究过这条规则，想看看它到底有没有道理。

sents.t: And the answer is, well, complicated.
sents.zh: 而答案嘛，有点复杂。

sents.t: You see, most bacteria attaches itself to food almost instantly.
sents.zh: 你看，大多数细菌几乎一瞬间就会附着到食物上。

sents.t: So even if you pick it up lightning quick, there's still probably gonna be some germs on there.
sents.zh: 所以就算你闪电般把它捡起来，上面多半还是会有一些细菌。

sents.t: Even so, we're sorry to say, but according to experts, the five second rule isn't real. Turns out, it's just a myth.
sents.zh: 即便如此，很遗憾地告诉你，专家说五秒规则不是真的。事实证明，它只是个谣言。

sents.t: Even the most delicious bite isn't worth a nasty bug.
sents.zh: 再好吃的一口，也不值得为它染上讨厌的病菌。

sents.t: And a few new ones at the end, like turns out, myth, and isn't worth. We'll look at those right now.
sents.zh: 最后还有几个新表达，比如 turns out、myth 和 isn't worth。我们马上来看看。

sents.t: In putting it together, we look at how some phrases work together, so you can say a complete idea.
sents.zh: 在“组合运用”这一部分，我们来看看一些短语怎么搭配使用，让你能完整地表达一个意思。

sents.t: Right. At the end of the dialogue, Lily says: it turns out the five second rule is just a myth.
sents.zh: 对。对话最后 Lily 说：事实证明，五秒规则只是个谣言。

sents.t: Let's start with turns out.
sents.zh: 我们先从 turns out 开始。

sents.t: Turns out. Turns out.
sents.zh: Turns out（结果是；原来）。Turns out。

sents.t: We say it turns out when we learn something new, and often it's a surprise. What we thought before was wrong.
sents.zh: 当我们得知一件新事情，而且往往出乎意料、之前想的是错的时候，就说 it turns out。

sents.t: Example one. I thought the restaurant was closed, but it turns out it's open until ten.
sents.zh: 例一。我以为那家餐厅关门了，结果它开到十点。

sents.t: Example two. Turns out, my client was allergic to the glue. We had to switch to a sensitive one.
sents.zh: 例二。原来我的客人对胶水过敏。我们只好换成敏感肌专用的。

sents.t: And now, myth.
sents.zh: 接下来是 myth。

sents.t: Myth. Myth.
sents.zh: Myth（谣言；迷思）。Myth。

sents.t: A myth is an idea that many people believe, but it's not true.
sents.zh: Myth 是很多人都相信、但其实不是真的的说法。

sents.t: Very natural. Now, here are two more from the dialogue: you can never be sure, and way better than.
sents.zh: 很地道。下面再来两个对话里的表达：you can never be sure 和 way better than。

sents.t: You can never be sure means there's always a little chance you're wrong.
sents.zh: You can never be sure 的意思是，你总有一点可能是错的，永远没法百分之百确定。

sents.t: And way better than means much better than. Way is a casual word for much, or a lot.
sents.zh: Way better than 就是 much better than，好得多。Way 是 much 或 a lot 的口语说法。

sents.t: Or, two seconds is way better than twenty seconds. But you can never be sure.
sents.zh: 或者：两秒比二十秒好得多。但你永远没法确定。

sents.t: And then Lily gives Mark some advice: you're better off throwing it out.
sents.zh: 然后 Lily 给了 Mark 一个建议：你最好还是把它扔掉。

sents.t: You're better off means this choice is better for you. It's a really common way to give advice.
sents.zh: You're better off 的意思是这个选择对你更好。这是给建议时非常常用的说法。

sents.t: You're better off booking early. My Saturday spots fill up fast.
sents.zh: 你最好早点预约。我周六的时段很快就约满了。

sents.t: And the last one: isn't worth.
sents.zh: 最后一个：isn't worth。

sents.t: If something isn't worth something, it's not a good trade. What you get is smaller than what you lose.
sents.zh: 如果某件事 isn't worth 另一件事，就是不划算：得到的比失去的少。

sents.t: One french fry isn't worth getting sick.
sents.zh: 为了一根薯条生病不值得。

sents.t: Or, from the lesson: even the most delicious bite isn't worth a nasty bug.
sents.zh: 或者课文里的：再好吃的一口，也不值得为它染上讨厌的病菌。

sents.t: So let's put it all together. Let's listen to a few examples.
sents.zh: 我们来把这些组合起来。听几个例子吧。

sents.t: Example one. I thought it was true, but it turns out it's just a myth.
sents.zh: 例一。我以为那是真的，结果原来只是个谣言。

sents.t: Example two. The floor looks relatively clean, but you can never be sure. You're better off throwing it out.
sents.zh: 例二。地板看起来比较干净，但你永远没法确定。你最好还是扔掉。

sents.t: Example three. Five seconds is way better than a minute. But one cookie isn't worth getting sick.
sents.zh: 例三。五秒比一分钟好得多。但为了一块饼干生病可不值得。

sents.t: Now let's do fluency builder. These are phrases that help you sound more natural, the way people really talk.
sents.zh: 现在来做“流利表达”。这些短语能让你听起来更自然，更像人们平时真正说话的样子。

sents.t: Phrase one. Just because it looks clean, doesn't mean it's clean.
sents.zh: 短语一。看起来干净，不代表真的干净。

sents.t: Just because it looks clean, doesn't mean it's clean. This pattern is so useful. Just because something, doesn't mean something else.
sents.zh: 看起来干净，不代表真的干净。这个句型太好用了：Just because 某事，doesn't mean 另一件事。

sents.t: Just because he's quiet doesn't mean he's angry. Just because it's expensive doesn't mean it's good.
sents.zh: 他不说话，不代表他生气了。贵的不一定就好。

sents.t: Phrase two. This one is from the original lesson, and it uses the word littering.
sents.zh: 短语二。这个来自原课文，用到了 littering 这个词。

sents.t: Dust, dirt, hair, crumbs, or whatever else might be littering the floor.
sents.zh: 灰尘、泥土、头发、碎屑，或者其他任何可能散落在地板上的东西。

sents.t: Littering. Littering the floor.
sents.zh: Littering（乱扔；散落）。Littering the floor（散落一地）。

sents.t: To litter usually means to throw trash on the ground in a public place. Like, don't litter in the park.
sents.zh: Litter 通常是指在公共场所往地上乱扔垃圾。比如：不要在公园乱扔垃圾。

sents.t: But here, littering the floor means lying all over the floor, like trash.
sents.zh: 但在这里，littering the floor 的意思是像垃圾一样散落满地。

sents.t: Crumbs are the very small pieces that fall from bread or cookies. At the end of a long day, the break room floor is littered with crumbs.
sents.zh: Crumbs 是面包或饼干掉下来的小碎屑。忙了一整天下来，休息室的地上满是碎屑。

sents.t: And in a salon, there's so much hair. And lash extensions! I find them everywhere. On my sweater, in my bag, on the floor.
sents.zh: 美容店里头发可多了。还有嫁接睫毛！我到处都能发现它们：毛衣上、包里、地上。

sents.t: Ha! Okay, phrase three is about no matter how.
sents.zh: 哈！好，短语三是关于 no matter how 的。

sents.t: Experts don't recommend the five second rule, no matter how clean a floor might seem.
sents.zh: 不管地板看起来多干净，专家都不建议遵循五秒规则。

sents.t: No matter how clean, no matter how fast, no matter how hungry you are. It means it doesn't change anything.
sents.zh: 不管多干净，不管多快，不管你有多饿。意思是这些都改变不了什么。

sents.t: No matter how tired I am, I always take off my makeup before bed.
sents.zh: 不管多累，我睡前都一定会卸妆。

sents.t: That's a good habit. Okay, Paula, before we listen again, I want to talk about this topic a little more.
sents.zh: 这是个好习惯。好，Paula，在我们再听一遍之前，我想多聊聊这个话题。

sents.t: Yes, let's. Ethan, did you know there was a real study about this? Scientists really did it.
sents.zh: 好啊。Ethan，你知道吗，真的有一项关于这个的研究。科学家真的做过实验。

sents.t: I read about that. Researchers in the United States dropped different foods on different surfaces, and they timed it. Less than one second, five seconds, thirty seconds, five minutes.
sents.zh: 我读到过。美国的研究人员把不同的食物丢到不同的表面上，然后计时。不到一秒、五秒、三十秒、五分钟。

sents.t: And what did they find?
sents.zh: 那他们发现了什么？

sents.t: Kind of what the lesson says. Some bacteria got onto the food in less than one second. So the five second rule is a myth.
sents.zh: 差不多就是课文说的那样。有些细菌不到一秒就沾到了食物上。所以五秒规则是个谣言。

sents.t: But longer was worse, right?
sents.zh: 不过时间越长越糟，对吧？

sents.t: Right. The longer it stays on the floor, the more bacteria it collects. So five seconds is way better than five minutes. But it's not zero.
sents.zh: 对。食物在地上待得越久，沾上的细菌就越多。所以五秒比五分钟好得多。但并不是零。

sents.t: What about different floors? I always think carpet is the dirtiest.
sents.zh: 那不同的地面呢？我一直觉得地毯最脏。

sents.t: The lesson says clean, dry floors usually have fewer germs than wet, textured surfaces like carpets. But the study found something surprising. Carpet moved fewer bacteria to the food than tile. So, it's complicated.
sents.zh: 课文说，干净干燥的地面上细菌通常比潮湿、有纹理的表面少，比如地毯。但研究发现了一件意外的事：地毯传到食物上的细菌反而比瓷砖少。所以，说来复杂。

sents.t: And the food matters too. Wet foods pick up more bacteria. Like watermelon. Watermelon was the worst one in the study.
sents.zh: 食物本身也有关系。湿的食物沾的细菌更多。比如西瓜。西瓜是研究里最糟的一个。

sents.t: Because it's wet and sticky?
sents.zh: 因为它又湿又黏？

sents.t: Exactly. Bacteria loves moisture. A dry cracker or a gummy candy picks up much less.
sents.zh: 没错。细菌喜欢潮湿。干饼干或者软糖沾到的就少得多。

sents.t: So if I drop a gummy bear on a dry kitchen floor, it's relatively safe?
sents.zh: 所以如果我把一颗小熊软糖掉在干燥的厨房地板上，相对来说是安全的？

sents.t: Relatively. But you can never be sure.
sents.zh: 相对安全。但你永远没法确定。

sents.t: Ha! You can never be sure. You learned the lesson.
sents.zh: 哈！你永远没法确定。你学会了。

sents.t: Okay, Paula, now you. Have you ever eaten something off the floor?
sents.zh: 好，Paula，该你了。你有没有吃过掉在地上的东西？

sents.t: Hmm. Honestly? Yes. At home, if it's my own kitchen, and the floor is dry, sometimes I do.
sents.zh: 嗯……说实话？吃过。在家里，如果是我自己的厨房，地板又是干的，有时候我会吃。

sents.t: Aha! Five second rule!
sents.zh: 啊哈！五秒规则！

sents.t: But never at work. At the studio, I'm really careful. If something touches the floor, a tweezer, a lash pad, anything, it goes in the trash or gets cleaned again.
sents.zh: 但工作的时候绝对不会。在工作室我特别小心。任何东西碰到地面，镊子、睫毛贴片，不管什么，要么扔进垃圾桶，要么重新消毒。

sents.t: That makes sense. You work so close to people's eyes.
sents.zh: 这很有道理。你的工作离别人的眼睛那么近。

sents.t: Exactly. Eyes are very sensitive. One dirty tool isn't worth an eye infection. And people walk around the studio all day, so the floor is bound to be dirty.
sents.zh: 没错。眼睛很敏感。为了一件脏工具让人眼睛感染，太不值得了。而且一整天都有人在工作室里走来走去，地板肯定很脏。

sents.t: You sound like Lily from the dialogue. Okay, my turn. I have an embarrassing story.
sents.zh: 你说话跟对话里的 Lily 一模一样。好，轮到我了。我有个尴尬的故事。

sents.t: Last summer, I was at a picnic, and I dropped a whole slice of pizza on the grass. Face down.
sents.zh: 去年夏天我去野餐，结果把一整块披萨掉在了草地上。还是正面朝下。

sents.t: Oh no. Face down is the worst.
sents.zh: 哦不。正面朝下最惨了。

sents.t: It was terrible. And everybody was watching. I picked it up lightning quick and said, five second rule!
sents.zh: 太惨了。而且大家都在看。我闪电般把它捡起来，说：五秒规则！

sents.t: Did you eat it?
sents.zh: 那你吃了吗？

sents.t: I looked at it. It had grass on it, a little dirt, and I think an ant.
sents.zh: 我看了看它。上面有草，有点土，我觉得还有一只蚂蚁。

sents.t: Ew! An ant attached itself to your pizza.
sents.zh: 咦！一只蚂蚁附着在你的披萨上了。

sents.t: It did! So I said, okay, this isn't worth it, and I threw it out. My friend gave me another slice.
sents.zh: 真的！所以我说，好吧，这不值得，然后就扔了。我朋友又给了我一块。

sents.t: Good choice. I think most people say five second rule as a joke anyway. So, what's the takeaway for our listeners?
sents.zh: 明智的选择。我觉得大多数人说五秒规则本来也就是开个玩笑。那么，我们想让听众记住什么呢？

sents.t: I think it's this. If the food is wet, or the floor is busy, or you're not at home, you're better off throwing it out.
sents.zh: 我觉得是这样：如果食物是湿的，或者地面人来人往，或者你不在家，那你最好还是扔掉。

sents.t: And if it's a dry cracker on your clean kitchen floor? It's probably fine, but it's your choice.
sents.zh: 那如果是一块干饼干，掉在你干净的厨房地板上呢？大概没事，不过看你自己选择。

sents.t: Exactly. Your floor, your choice.
sents.zh: 没错。你的地板，你做主。

sents.t: Okay, I think we're ready to listen to the dialogue again. This time it's a little slower, so try to catch all the phrases we talked about.
sents.zh: 好，我觉得我们可以再听一遍对话了。这次会稍微慢一点，试着把我们讲过的短语都听出来。

sents.t: Mark, did you just eat that french fry off the floor?
sents.zh: Mark，你刚才是不是把地上那根薯条吃了？

sents.t: Five second rule! I picked it up lightning quick.
sents.zh: 五秒规则！我闪电般就捡起来了。

sents.t: You picked it up and just stuffed it in your mouth. That's so gross.
sents.zh: 你捡起来就直接塞进嘴里了。太恶心了。

sents.t: Come on, it was only on the floor for like two seconds. Is there any truth to the five second rule, or not?
sents.zh: 拜托，它在地上也就待了两秒左右。五秒规则到底有没有道理啊？

sents.t: Well, believe it or not, scientists actually studied it, to see if there's anything to it.
sents.zh: 嗯，信不信由你，科学家还真研究过这个，想看看它到底有没有点道理。

sents.t: Really? And what did they find?
sents.zh: 真的吗？那他们发现了什么？

sents.t: The answer is, well, complicated. Most bacteria attaches itself to food almost instantly.
sents.zh: 答案嘛，有点复杂。大多数细菌几乎是一瞬间就会附着到食物上。

sents.t: Instantly? So even if I'm super fast, there are still germs on it?
sents.zh: 一瞬间？所以就算我手超快，上面还是有细菌？

sents.t: Probably, yeah. And this is the front of the studio. Clients walk here all day. It's bound to be dirty.
sents.zh: 多半是的。而且这里是工作室的前厅，客人一整天都在这儿走来走去。肯定很脏。

sents.t: But the floor looks clean. We mopped it this morning.
sents.zh: 可是地板看起来很干净啊。我们今天早上才拖过。

sents.t: Just because a floor looks clean doesn't mean it's bacteria free. Some bacteria is super resistant.
sents.zh: 地板看起来干净，不代表上面就没有细菌。有些细菌的抵抗力超强。

sents.t: Okay, but most germs are harmless, right?
sents.zh: 好吧，但大多数细菌都是无害的，对吧？

sents.t: A lot of them are. But some can make you sick, ranging from a bad cold to something downright dangerous. You can never be sure.
sents.zh: 很多是无害的。但有些会让你生病，轻的是重感冒，重的可能真的很危险。你永远没法确定。

sents.t: Fine. But two seconds is still way better than twenty seconds.
sents.zh: 行吧。不过两秒总比二十秒好得多吧。

sents.t: Sure. But it turns out the five second rule is just a myth. Next time, you're better off throwing it out.
sents.zh: 那当然。但事实证明，五秒规则只是个谣言。下次你最好还是直接扔掉。

sents.t: You're right. One french fry isn't worth getting sick. Can I have one of yours?
sents.zh: 你说得对。为了一根薯条生病不值得。能给我一根你的吗？

sents.t: Ha! Only if you wash your hands first.
sents.zh: 哈！先去洗手才行。

sents.t: Okay, so Mark learned his lesson, I think.
sents.zh: 好，我觉得 Mark 这下长记性了。

sents.t: I hope so. And he still got a french fry in the end. If he washes his hands.
sents.zh: 希望如此。而且他最后还是吃到了薯条——前提是他去洗手。

sents.t: Ha! Lily is strict. So, Paula, after all this, will you still use the five second rule?
sents.zh: 哈！Lily 好严格。那 Paula，听了这么多，你以后还会用五秒规则吗？

sents.t: At home, maybe, with dry food. But now I'll think about the bacteria every time.
sents.zh: 在家里也许会，干的食物吧。但现在每次我都会想到细菌了。

sents.t: Listeners, here's a little challenge for you this week. The next time someone drops food and says five second rule, tell them what you learned.
sents.zh: 各位听众，这周给你们一个小挑战：下次有人掉了吃的、说“五秒规则”的时候，把你学到的告诉他们。

sents.t: You can say: Believe it or not, it's just a myth. Most bacteria attaches itself to food almost instantly.
sents.zh: 你可以说：信不信由你，这只是个谣言。大多数细菌几乎一瞬间就会附着到食物上。

sents.t: Or, you're better off throwing it out. It isn't worth getting sick.
sents.zh: 或者说：你最好还是扔掉吧。为这个生病不值得。

sents.t: Thank you so much for listening to Open Talk.
sents.zh: 非常感谢收听 Open Talk。

sents.t: We'll be back soon with another everyday conversation, and more useful English.
sents.zh: 我们很快会带着另一段日常对话和更多实用英语回来。

sents.t: Until next time, goodbye!
sents.zh: 下次见，再见！

sents.t: Bye everyone! And wash your hands!
sents.zh: 大家再见！记得洗手哦！
